rows.name: Prefer nonstop flights
rows.rationale: Most independent examples state or imply that nonstop is preferred, including 'non-stop is always preferred,' 'definitely a non-stop,' and 'a nonstop flight.' One example allows a layover when it is cheaper but limits it to one layover, and another requests a midway stopover for coast-to-coast travel. Together, these support a scoped synthetic habit: default to nonstop when practical, but allow a single layover for savings or a stopover for long-flight comfort.

However, the one-layover price tolerance and the midway stopover for a coast-to-coast flight are each only one-off current-trip details, so they should not be promoted to reusable defaults.
